quick: Induction ~2-2.5 mg/kg IV (titrate ~40 mg every 10 s); maintenance/sedation by infusion
Decades of data show no clear teratogenic risk; neonatal depression possible at delivery
Small amounts in milk; generally compatible after recovery
No specific adjustment; titrate to effect
Continuous airway, oxygenation, BP, ECG; triglycerides/CK if prolonged
summary: Propofol is a short-acting intravenous general anesthetic and sedative that enhances inhibitory GABA-A signaling. It is used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia (>=3 years for induction, >=2 months for maintenance), monitored anesthesia care sedation, and ICU sedation of intubated, mechanically ventilated adults. It must be given only by clinicians trained in anesthesia/airway management with continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, because it causes dose-dependent hypotension and apnea. It is contraindicated in patients with egg or soy anaphylaxis. Prolonged high-dose infusion risks propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS); strict aseptic technique is essential as the lipid emulsion supports microbial growth.
indications: Induction of general anesthesia in patients >= 3 years of age
Maintenance of general anesthesia in patients >= 2 months of age
Initiation and maintenance of monitored anesthesia care (MAC) sedation in adults
Sedation for adults in combination with regional anesthesia
ICU sedation of intubated, mechanically ventilated adult patients

dosage.d: ~2-2.5 mg/kg IV, titrated in ~40 mg boluses every 10 seconds to effect
Infusion ~100-200 mcg/kg/min (6-12 mg/kg/h), or intermittent boluses

dosage.n: Avoid rapid bolus, especially in elderly

dosage.d: Infusion ~5-50 mcg/kg/min, titrated to target sedation
dosage.n: Use lowest effective rate; watch for PRIS with high-dose/prolonged use

dosage.d: Lower induction dose and slower maintenance rate
dosage.n: Avoid rapid bolus to limit cardiorespiratory depression

admin: Administer ONLY by persons trained in general anesthesia/airway management and not performing the procedure
Maintain continuous monitoring of oxygenation, ventilation, blood pressure and ECG with resuscitation equipment immediately available
Use strict aseptic technique; the emulsion supports microbial growth - begin promptly and complete administration within 12 hours of opening a vial; one vial per patient
Shake well; inspect for phase separation and discard if present; flush lines to avoid incompatibilities
Titrate slowly, especially in the elderly and hemodynamically fragile, to limit hypotension and apnea
moa: Like other general anesthetics, propofol's mechanism is incompletely understood, but it is believed to produce sedation and anesthesia mainly by positively modulating the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA at ligand-gated GABA-A receptors, increasing chloride conductance and CNS inhibition. Onset is rapid (about one arm-brain circulation, ~40 seconds) and recovery is fast due to rapid redistribution and clearance.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to propofol or any component
History of anaphylaxis to eggs, egg products, soybeans or soy products
relative: Compromised airway without ability to manage it
Prolonged high-dose ICU infusion (PRIS risk), especially in children
monitor: Continuous oxygenation, ventilation, blood pressure, ECG
Triglycerides and acid-base/CK/potassium with prolonged infusion

preg: Data over several decades have not identified a clear drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage; most exposures are at cesarean delivery, where neonatal depression can occur. Anesthetic/sedative use beyond 3 hours during peak fetal brain development is of theoretical concern (animal data). Use when needed with appropriate monitoring.
lact: Small amounts of propofol appear in breast milk; given its rapid clearance, breastfeeding can generally resume once the mother has recovered from anesthesia.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment; titrate to clinical effect.

major: Opioids and sedatives (benzodiazepines, barbiturates) - markedly potentiate anesthetic/sedative and cardiorespiratory depression; reduce propofol dose
In pediatric patients, concomitant fentanyl can cause serious bradycardia
moderate: Potent inhalational anesthetics (isoflurane, sevoflurane, desflurane) - additive anesthetic and cardiorespiratory depression
Valproate - increases propofol blood levels; reduce propofol dose and monitor
minor: No clinically significant change in onset/duration of common neuromuscular blockers
interactions.diagnostics: Lipid emulsion can raise serum triglycerides with prolonged infusion; PRIS is associated with metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis (raised CK) and renal failure.

serious: Propofol infusion syndrome (metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalemia, cardiac/renal failure)

monitoring: Continuous monitoring of oxygenation, ventilation, blood pressure and ECG throughout
Early signs of hypotension, apnea, airway obstruction or desaturation, especially after bolus dosing
Triglycerides, acid-base status, potassium and CK during prolonged/high-dose infusion
Recovery of mental alertness after the procedure
counsel: This is a hospital anesthetic given through a vein by anesthesia-trained staff
You may feel a brief stinging at the injection site as it goes in
You will be monitored closely; tell staff about any allergy to eggs or soy
Do not drive, operate machinery or sign legal documents for the rest of the day after sedation/anesthesia
Have a responsible adult take you home after outpatient procedures
pk: Rapid CNS effect; blood-brain equilibration ~1-3 minutes
Initial distribution very rapid; terminal half-life prolonged after long infusions due to tissue stores
Short - prompt awakening after brief use; prolonged after long high-dose infusions
Store at 4-25 C; do not freeze; shake well before use
pearls: For anesthesia/MAC, administer only by anesthesia-trained personnel with full monitoring and airway/resuscitation readiness
Contraindicated in patients with egg or soy anaphylaxis
Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS) - high-dose/prolonged infusion can cause fatal acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalemia and cardiac failure; use lowest effective rate
Lipid emulsion supports microbial growth - strict asepsis, one vial per patient, finish within 12 hours of opening
Causes dose-dependent hypotension and apnea, accentuated by rapid bolus and in the elderly
missed: Not applicable - propofol is administered as a titrated intravenous bolus and/or continuous infusion by clinicians in a monitored setting, not as a patient-administered scheduled dose.
overdose: Overdose causes cardiorespiratory depression. Stop propofol immediately. Treat respiratory depression with assisted ventilation and oxygen; treat cardiovascular depression by raising the legs, increasing IV fluids, and giving vasopressors and/or anticholinergic agents as needed. Provide full supportive care until the drug redistributes and is cleared.
